additions.reason: The light of Torah is explicitly the good counterpart to the darkness of Package 2. additions.reason: The candle (נֵר) that does not go out at night is the core image of Proverbs 31:18, which the Rebbe interprets as the Torah light that persists through the darkness of distancing. נֵר and אוֹר הַתּוֹרָה are bechinas of each other — both express the same persistent illumination from the Tzaddik's teaching.
additions.source_quote: שׁוּב לֹא יִכְבֶּה בַּלַּיְלָה נֵרָהּ ... כִּי לֹא יִכְבֶּה בַּלַּיְלָה נֵרָהּ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד

additions.source_quote: תֵּכֶף כְּשֶׁטּוֹעֲמִין טַעַם הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁל הַצַּדִּיק הָאֱמֶת

additions.reason: Merchandise (סְחוֹרָה) is explicitly glossed as the Tzaddik's Torah — 'שֶׁהַסְּחוֹרָה שֶׁלּוֹ, הַיְנוּ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁלּוֹ'. The word סְחוֹרָה is one of the synonyms or facets of the same concept: Torah knowledge as something that is tasted, traded, and permanently retained. It belongs to the good Torah-light package.
